title: Greenline Readiness Scorecard & Capacity Lockdown for Cross-Stack Cutover
creator: Anika Patel
description:
Purpose: Create a lightweight, operational readiness scorecard we call 'Greenline' that gates release train cutovers across runtime/console/api surfaces. The scorecard combines automated signals (capacity headroom, SLO burn rates, infra alerts) with manual readiness checks (oncall coverage, migrations complete, canary health) and produces an explicit 'Lockdown' action when thresholds are crossed. This ticket defines the scoring calculation, the lockdown gating thresholds, the stakeholder handoff choreography, and a thin UI/Slack signal for run-of-show calls.

Scope:
- Define signals and weighting for Greenline score (quant + qual).
- Specify capacity-lockdown rules and automated throttles when score < 0.6.
- Author a runbook for PM/Eng/Platform handoff during preflight and rollback windows.
- Implement dashboard widgets (Console) and a Slack bot ping for the release conductor.
- Validate with a simulated launch dry-run and measure gating false-positive rate.

Out of scope: runbook automation beyond initial throttles, long-term policy engine integration.

Why: Current release gates are fragmented across teams and lack a unified numeric signal. That causes inconsistent go/no-go decisions and ad-hoc rollbacks. Greenline aims to standardize the decision-making rubric and preserve customer availability while enabling predictable launches.
acceptance_criteria: Official Greenline scoring doc published in Confluence with signal definitions and weights
Capacity Lockdown rules implemented as runtime throttles (config flag) and tested in stage
Dashboard widget in Console surface shows live Greenline score and top 3 contributing signals
Slack bot posts preflight score 30/15/5 minutes before cutover and supports manual override by release conductor
Dry-run completed with <10% gating false positives and annotated postmortem
success_metrics: Reduction in last-minute rollbacks attributed to capacity issues by >= 40% in next quarter
Average decision time during cutover reduced from 18m to <7m
On-call escalations during first-hour post-cutover decreased by 30%
notes: Trade-offs discussed in kickoff: keep score computation simple to avoid brittleness; initial weighting favors automated capacity signals over noisy application-level errors
Decision: initial lockdown threshold set to 0.60; safety valve will be a hard throttle tier and not a full abort to avoid blocking dependent services
Open question: how to integrate Dedicated customer-specific capacity reservations (follow-up PM ticket required)
Concordance with SRE: agreed to surface burn-rate and error-budget percentiles as top signals (ENG-2714)
